title: A nonzero section with a zero has positive degree on a proper integral curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $C$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $s\in\Gamma(C,\mathcal L)$ be a nonzero global section. Then $\deg_k(\mathcal L)\ge0$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. If $s$ vanishes at some point of $C$, that is, if its nonvanishing locus $C_s$ of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] is not all of $C$, then $\deg_k(\mathcal L)>0$.

source.place: Tag 0B40, lemma-check-invertible-sheaf-trivial, clauses (1) and (2), with curve meaning integral separated finite type of dimension one.

proof.text: Put $D=Z(s)$, the zero scheme of $s$ from [def-pc-zero-scheme]. The local description in [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties] identifies the complement of the nonvanishing locus with the underlying support of $D$. Since $C$ is integral and $s$ is nonzero, [lem-pc-nonzero-section-integral-cartier] shows that $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor. By the definition of the nonvanishing locus in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], the hypothesis that $s$ vanishes at a point is exactly that $D$ is nonempty (equivalently $C_s\ne C$).

source.place: Tag 0B40, lemma-check-invertible-sheaf-trivial, proof before clauses (1) and (2), using the regular-section/effective-Cartier-divisor characterization

proof.text: The zero-scheme/divisor identification [lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso], applied to the section $s:\mathcal O_C\to\mathcal L$, gives an isomorphism $\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O_C(D)$. Isomorphic invertible modules have the same Euler characteristic and hence the same degree by [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], so $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\deg_k(\mathcal O_C(D))$.

source.place: Tag 0B40, proof of lemma-check-invertible-sheaf-trivial: the section identifies the line bundle with the divisor bundle

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-pc-degree-base-change] apply to $C$ and the effective Cartier divisor $D$: the given topological Krull dimension is one, and [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] identifies this with the local-ring dimension used by [def-pc-dimension]. Its effective-divisor clause therefore gives $\deg_k(\mathcal O_C(D))=\dim_k\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)$, with the right-hand side finite-dimensional over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0AYY, lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor, degree formula for an effective Cartier divisor

proof.text: A finite-dimensional vector space has nonnegative dimension, so the preceding equality proves $\deg_k(\mathcal L)\ge0$. If $D$ is nonempty, [lem-pc-cartier-divisor-finite-over-field] makes $D$ affine and finite over $k$; hence $\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional $k$-algebra (an affine nonempty scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A\ne0$), and its dimension is positive. Thus $\deg_k(\mathcal L)>0$ whenever $s$ vanishes at a point.

source.place: Tag 0AYY, proof of lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor, first sentences and the finite-over-the-field conclusion
